intro: Comparing amounts and saying something is equal: more books than, as many hours as, more than a hundred, the same as.
p.tanto.consejo: With a noun it changes: «tantos libros», «tantas horas». With a verb it does not: «no gasto tanto como tú».
p.tantas.consejo: It agrees with a feminine plural noun: «tantas horas como tú». «Como» comes after.
p.más de.consejo: Before a number you use «de», not «que»: «más de cien euros».
p.menos de.consejo: Like «más de»: «menos de mil euros». It goes before a number.
p.el mismo.consejo: It agrees with the noun: «el mismo horario». «Que» comes after: «el mismo horario que tú».
p.la misma.consejo: It is feminine: «la misma calle». Plural: «las mismas». It can take «que»: «la misma que tú».
p.igual que.consejo: It says two things are alike: «sonríe igual que él». It never changes.
p.el doble.consejo: You say «el doble de» something: «el doble de pan». It is masculine and singular.
p.la mitad.consejo: It is feminine although it ends in -d: «la mitad del pan». You do not say «el mitad».
p.ganar.consejo: It works for money and for matches: «gana mil euros» and «gana el partido». It is regular.
p.gastar.consejo: It is the opposite of saving: «gasto poco dinero». It is regular.
p.el precio.consejo: It is read PRE-thyo. Do not mix it up with «aprecio», which means affection.
p.el horario.consejo: It is masculine: «el horario». It is about hours: «el horario de la tienda».
p.al mes.consejo: With money you say «al mes»: «gana mil euros al mes». Also «al día» and «al año».
b1.texto:
With **nouns**:

- **más / menos + noun + que**: tengo **más** libros **que** tú.
- **tanto/a/os/as + noun + como**: trabajo **tantas** horas **como** tú. It agrees with the noun.

With **verbs**: trabaja **más que** yo; no gasto **tanto como** tú.

Before a **number**, «que» becomes **de**: **más de** cien euros, **menos de** mil.

To say something is the same: **el mismo** horario **que** tú, **la misma** profesora **que** tú, **igual que** él. And also: **el doble**, **la mitad**.
b2.f0.texto: Do you work as many hours as your brother?
b2.f1.texto: No, he works more than me.
b2.f2.texto: Does he earn more than you?
b2.f3.texto: No, he earns less than me.
b2.f4.texto: How much does he earn per month?
b2.f5.texto: He earns less than a thousand euros a month.
b2.f6.texto: I have the same schedule as you, but I do not spend as much as you.
b2.f7.texto: My flat costs more than eight hundred euros a month.
b4.texto:
Choose the pattern according to what you compare:

- **más / menos + noun + que**: Tengo más libros que tú.
- **tanto/a/os/as + noun + como**: Trabajo tantas horas como tú.
- **tan + adjective + como**: El café está tan caliente como el té.
- **verb + más / menos que**, or **tanto como**: Gana menos que yo. No gasto tanto como tú.
- **más / menos de + number**: Cuesta más de cien euros.

For what is identical: **el mismo… que**, **la misma… que**, **igual que**. To multiply and divide: **el doble**, **la mitad**.
b4.e0.texto: I have more books than you.
b4.e1.texto: I work as many hours as you.
b4.e2.texto: It costs more than a hundred euros.
b5.f0.texto: Two old bakeries open their doors in the same street.
b5.f1.texto: The one on the corner bakes twice as much bread as the other.
b5.f2.texto: Its oven works as many hours as the summer sun.
b5.f3.texto: The smell of warm bread fills more corners than the wind.
b5.f4.texto: The neighbours queue from six in the morning.
b5.f5.texto: In the other bakery, a man counts the coins patiently.
b5.f6.texto: His bread costs half of what the one on the corner costs.
b5.f7.texto: The baker earns less than his neighbour, but he smiles just like him.
b5.f8.texto: At dusk, the two shops close with the same golden light.
b5.f9.texto: The two men greet each other from the door, like old friends.
b6.o0.refuerzo: Yes! Libros is masculine plural, and tanto agrees with it.
b6.o1.refuerzo: «Tan» goes before an adjective, not a noun.
b7.o0.refuerzo: That is it! Before a number comes «de».
b7.o1.refuerzo: «Que» compares two things, not a number.
b8.traduccion: I do not spend as much as you
b9.o0.refuerzo: «Profesora» is feminine, so «el» does not fit.
b9.o1.refuerzo: «Lo mismo» is «the same thing», with no noun after it.
b9.o2.refuerzo: Well done! Feminine singular: la misma profesora.
b10.pregunta: Write in Spanish: «He works more than me.»
b11.o0.refuerzo: «El doble» is twice the amount, the opposite.
b11.o1.refuerzo: «El mismo» says that something is identical.
b11.o2.refuerzo: Correct! One of two equal parts.
b12.frase: El café está ____ caliente como el té.
b12.o0.refuerzo: «Tanto» goes with a verb or a noun.
b12.o1.refuerzo: Yes! Before an adjective you use «tan».
b12.o2.refuerzo: «Tanta» agrees with a feminine noun, not with an adjective.
b12.pregunta: Which word goes before an adjective?
p.gasto.consejo: From «gastar», to spend money. The -o ending means «I».
p.ochocientos.consejo: Ocho means eight. The c before e is a «th» in Spain.
p.panaderías.consejo: The í keeps the i and a apart, so say RI-as in two syllables.
p.hornea.consejo: From «hornear», to bake. The h is silent, and e and a are separate.
p.rincones.consejo: A starting r is strong, and the c before o sounds like «th».
p.hombres.consejo: Plural of «hombre». The h is silent, the b sounds soft.
p.viejos.consejo: The v sounds like b, and the j sounds like h.
p.tantos.consejo: Its feminine form is «tantas». Use it to compare amounts.
